answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with an aging bond: a new identity posts a nonrefundable deposit locked until it has a long, public work history, so its anchor on the ledger is costly to forge. A rotating lantern of randomly chosen peers audits a sample of claimants each round and slashes any fake found. The ivory registry allows one aging anchor per funded principal, so k puppets need k deposits locked for months and face k independent audit chances. Cost scales linearly with the number of keys while each fake vote stays capped, so flooding the economy never pays.
